profile_text.body:
OpenAI's site at chatgpt.com presents ChatGPT as a single place to answer questions, write, create images, complete work, and code, offered free to start or through a downloadable app. The company describes ChatGPT as helping users get answers, find inspiration, and be more productive, and notes that chats may be reviewed and used to improve its AI models. The profile record lists OpenAI as a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Beyond ChatGPT, the tracked products include the OpenAI API and GPT models, the OpenAI Playground and Dashboard for API testing, fine-tuning, usage tracking, and team management, Operator as an autonomous web agent, DALL-E for image generation, Sora for video generation, and the Whisper API for speech recognition, transcription, and translation. Notes attached to those entries flag usage-based cost escalation for the API and dashboard, credential exposure and action authorization for Operator, IP provenance for DALL-E, and provenance and disclosure for Sora.

The litigation record lists twelve cases involving OpenAI entities across federal district courts and one appeals court, including Gourley v. OPENAI FOUNDATION and Mall v. OPENAI FOUNDATION in the N.D. Florida, Starr v. OpenAI Group PBC and Byrd v. OpenAI, Inc. in the N.D. California, wikiHow, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. in the S.D. New York, two United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC matters in the E.D. Arkansas, Haugland v. OpenAI, Inc. in the D. Hawaii, Craddock v. OpenAi OpCo LLC in the N.D. California, Office of the Attorney General, State of Florida, Department of Legal Affairs v. OpenAI Global, LLC in the S.D. Florida, Couture v. Openai Global, LLC in the S.D. California, and X.AI Corp., et al. v. OpenAI, Inc., et al. before the Ninth Circuit. California accounts for 281 entries in that exposure record. Eleven MCP servers referencing OpenAI are also listed, among them one that wraps image and audio generation endpoints and several agent entries covering authentication, LangChain orchestration, structured output, and tracing.
